decision: reuse orders as the single store for Falabella and Ripley
why: orders already owns the internal ID, seller-scoped external identity, items, events, and snapshots

decision: keep order synchronization separate from automatic invoicing
why: they have different schedules, controls, failure modes, and effects

decision: use a five-day initial window and cursor-based incremental updates afterward
why: limits first-load cost while retaining the existing efficient overlap model

decision: Use the incremental account-level scheduler as the base and graft explicit item completeness, unmapped states, and canonical stock identity
why: Falabella legacy inbox, lifecycle, labels, and billing still depend on provider tables, while orders and channel accounts already provide the canonical seam
evidence: Cross-judge selected candidate B and rejected a full provider-framework rewrite for this release

decision: Expose one generic sync status and trigger contract for both channels
why: The unified page must not know provider-specific scheduler endpoints
evidence: GET /order-management/sync-status returns account states and POST /order-management/sync triggers one or all eligible accounts

why: Public Peru docs confirm the production Mirakl host but do not justify inferring sandbox or QA labels from hostnames
evidence: packages/web/src/routes/PedidosRipley.tsx and packages/server/src/ripley-api-url.js updated to show only the configured tenant

decision: Add a reusable order-sync verification command
why: The feature crosses DB, scheduler, provider adapters, and UI, so a single repeatable check is safer than manual spot checks
result: builds, backend tests, web tests, typecheck, and architecture invariants passed

decision: Preview-load the existing local /orders route without starting backend workers
why: The visible preview was already on port 3011, but its API target on port 3012 was not running and the app showed login
result: visual authenticated inspection deferred; no scheduler was started against real credentials

decision: Run the Ripley synchronizer against the configured read-only OR11 API and local PostgreSQL
why: Unit fixtures cannot prove the tenant accepts the final paging and date parameters
evidence: Run 9 received and upserted 49 complete orders with zero order failures

decision: Preserve local rows created by the first live probe even though some were older orders updated inside the window
why: Deleting user-visible database rows was not authorized
evidence: The final code filters first load by createdAt; 49 local rows remain and the unified page defaults to today's date

decision: Treat a persisted Ripley header without order_lines as a partial run
why: Advancing the cursor could otherwise strand an incomplete order after the overlap expires
evidence: New test failed before the fix and passes after; the header commits, the cursor stays, and the order is retried

decision: Remove the legacy company-plus-external-order uniqueness from canonical stock jobs
why: The same external ID can exist in Falabella and Ripley for one company
evidence: Canonical jobs are unique by orders.id; only null-order legacy jobs use a partial compatibility key

decision: Request connectedOnly orders from the unified page
why: The seller selector already hid inactive or credentialless sellers, but the SQL list could still include their marketplace rows
evidence: A failing-before query test now proves active accounts and required channel credentials are enforced by SQL

decision: Bound provider requests and recover abandoned running rows under the account advisory lock
why: A killed process can leave run history marked running, and an unbounded provider request can hold one concurrency slot forever
evidence: Falabella and Ripley sync fetches have a 60 second request timeout; the next locked run closes interrupted rows before starting

decision: Run no-comments and audit new suppressions
why: The Comment Sicko rerun returned no usable report, so the automated comment review failed open and required a manual scoped scan
evidence: Deleted one redundant RipleyOrder doc comment; no new lint or TypeScript suppressions remain

decision: Run the reusable full verification lever and inspect the real schema
why: The handoff requires executable proof across provider, server, UI, build, and database identity
evidence: 226 server tests passed with one skipped integration, 34 web tests passed, all builds passed, and PostgreSQL shows separate canonical and legacy stock indexes

decision: Inspect the unified route in the collaborative browser
why: Visual verification requires an authenticated session and starting the API workers can call configured marketplace and billing integrations
evidence: The app and login render on port 3011; authenticated /orders composition remains uninspected in the browser

decision: Repeat the complete verification after timeout, recovery, and connected-seller refinements
why: The earlier proof preceded the final concurrency recovery and filtering changes
evidence: 229 of 230 server tests passed with one intentional skip, 34 web tests passed, all builds and architecture invariants passed; git diff --check is clean
